Bb #1134 (CC30) numbers: Win10 header is 24 px in every fixture, including one whose font is 13 px high. i7 gives 20 (an 8x16 stand-in font plus 2*2 edge). Stock comctl32 _Header_InitTheme (RVA 0x85d98, read from the corpus) calls GetThemePartSize for parts 1, 5, 4 and 7 (state 0, TS_TRUE) and GetThemePosition(1, 0, 0xd4b). These calls are the header's probe list.

Trap for the table design: Theme.active is overloaded. keyFindings: Committed as 5cf13a5 (only this file, not pushed). 494 lines. Based on about 837 uxtheme functions pulled from the corpus (all callees within 4 levels of the 156 distinct export bodies), plus bytes read through /api/bytes. Wine was run for nothing; no Windows run.

Default GetThemeAppProperties on Win10 is 3 (STAP_ALLOW_NONCLIENT|STAP_ALLOW_CONTROLS), from CAppInfo::CAppInfo @0x37ac. The Industrial7 crate w10-uxtheme-off uses 7, which is a divergence. SetThemeAppProperties(0) makes every OpenThemeData fail with LastError 0x80070490. It does not change IsThemeActive or IsAppThemed.
EnableTheming (ordinals 36 and 129, one body at 0x4f7c0) is a no-op that returns S_OK. Wine's version differs: it persists ThemeActive=0 in the registry.

HTHEME is not a pointer. It is (generation<<16)|slot into g_pRenderList (0x28-byte entries). A bad or stale handle gives E_HANDLE 0x80070006. A second OpenThemeData with the same parameters returns the same HTHEME, so each open needs its own close. CloseThemeData(NULL) is E_HANDLE by inference. Many failures call SetLastError with an HRESULT, so GetLastError reads 0x80070490, not 1168.

Property getters check the output pointer (E_POINTER) before the handle (E_HANDLE). GetThemePartSize checks the handle first, then psz. GetThemeColor and GetThemeInt are the same body (RVA 0x1cf80). GetThemeMetric is the colour lookup followed by MulDiv(v, dpi, 96) via ScaleThemeSize.

GetThemePartSize: border-fill parts give TS_MIN max(1,2*border) and TS_TRUE 2*border+1, and TS_DRAW is E_INVALIDARG. Image parts use content margins for TS_MIN and the DPI-selected DIB frame size for TS_TRUE. Only the pieces needed for TS_MIN, TS_TRUE and TS_DRAW were read. So a header height needs image or margin data, and a recorded-constants table must model the image-versus-border-fill split and DPI plateaus.

OpenThemeData class-list parsing: a string stored in window property 0xa910 (SetWindowTheme's pszSubIdList) replaces the whole class list. 0xa911 is the app name. The list is split on ';' and the first success wins. 'App::Class' splits on the first '::'. In dark mode the app name becomes 'DarkMode' or 'DarkMode_<app>'. Matching is ASCII case-insensitive. The failure code is 0x80070490.

OpenThemeData gate order: NULL class list gives E_POINTER, a bad hwnd gives E_HANDLE, then the hook-state gate, then the app-flag gate (both 0x80070490), then an empty string gives E_INVALIDARG, then the section open. Under high contrast, unless the app opts in, all Open variants return NULL and leave LastError untouched. OpenThemeDataForDpi with dpi above 480 gives LastError 0x57. A screen DPI other than 96 forces OTD_FORCE_RECT_SIZING.

Data layers: msstyles is opened only by a few file-based calls (GetThemeDocumentationProperty, GetThemeDefaults, EnumThemes, EnumThemeColors, EnumThemeSizes, EnumThemeProperties, OpenThemeDataFromFile). LoadThemeLibrary uses LoadLibraryExW as data file and requires resource PACKTHEM_VERSION to equal 4. Every normal call reads two kernel sections named from \Sessions\N\Windows\ThemeSection. The section header is the magic BEGINTHM plus version 0x10007, with a class index of 0x18-byte entries at hdr+0x3c. The loader and ALPC service are not needed to read values.

Theme service ALPC port \ThemeApiPort, opcodes: 1 QueryThemeServices, 2 GetCurrentChangeNumber (falls back to ROOTSECTION+0x410 when the service is absent), 3 LoadGlobalTheme, 4 ProcessAssignSection, 0x3ed AcquireOrAddTheme, 0x3ee ReleaseTheme, 0x3ef Reestablish. A missing service gives IsCompositionActive FALSE and 0x8007041D for global theme changes. Ordinary reads still work if the sections exist.

Ordinals: 108 ordinal-only exports, 34 of them SHUNIMPL forwarders. All other ordinals are identified from the PDB function names, with a signature or behaviour note for about half. Correction to the brief: in 19041 AllowDarkModeForWindow is ordinal 133, and 135 is SetPreferredAppMode. Also covered: 132 ShouldAppsUseDarkMode, 136 FlushMenuThemes, 137 IsDarkModeAllowedForWindow, 138 ShouldSystemUseDarkMode, 139 IsDarkModeAllowedForApp. Mode semantics: AllowDarkModeForWindow stores window property 0xa91e with the string 'Enabled'; IsDarkModeAllowedForWindow is FALSE unless the mode is 1 or 2; g_preferredAppMode starts at 0.

GetThemeSys*: with a NULL hTheme, GetThemeSysColor, SysColorBrush, SysSize, SysFont and SysBool fall back to classic user32 values, but GetThemeSysInt and GetThemeSysString return E_HANDLE. A themed GetThemeSysColorBrush returns a brush the caller owns. SM-to-TMT size mapping is verified against Wine's vssym32.h: 1201..1210. Sys fonts are 801..809 and sys strings 1401..1404.

Other recorded behaviour: SetWindowTheme with an invalid hwnd (including NULL) is E_HANDLE, stores atoms ('$' for an empty string) and sends WM_THEMECHANGED with wParam -1 and lParam 0x80000001. DrawThemeParentBackground returns S_FALSE on re-entry through property 0xa915. Buffered paint uses a per-thread TLS pool, and BeginBufferedPaint does an implicit ThreadAddRef. cbSize must be 0x18 for paint params and 0x10 for animation params. EndBufferedPaint(NULL) is E_INVALIDARG, and unknown or other-thread handles are E_FAIL. The theme-hook install list excludes wininit, winlogon, lsass, services, svchost, dfssvc, winmgmt, spoolsv, msdtc and ntvdm. uxtheme loads comctl32 v6 itself through its own activation context.

comctl32 Header_NewFont @0x86174 calls GetThemeTextExtent(hTheme, hdc, part 1, state 0, L"M", -1, 0x800, ...) and falls back to GetTextExtentPointW when that fails. The header-height 24-versus-20 root cause belongs to the survey and probe roles. Only the uxtheme-side behaviour is fixed here.

keyFindings: Wine is not a Win10 oracle for uxtheme. It is a headless smoke test and plumbing check. Its data comes from Wine's own authored theme (light.msstyles in Proton and Ubuntu, aero.msstyles in the 11.18 source tree), not Microsoft's. No Microsoft .msstyles exists on this host or in the corpus API.

Header height is 20 px (system font) or 17 px (DEFAULT_GUI_FONT) in every combination I ran. The combinations were comctl32 v5 and v6, theme on and off, Proton wine 11.0 and system wine 9.0. Wine's comctl32 never uses the theme: header.c:1636 and :2095 set nHeight = tmHeight + 4. Industrial7's 20 px matches Wine's value, so Wine reproduces the Industrial7 symptom and not Win10.

Win10 gets 24 from the theme. Header_OnLayout (decomp) takes max(textCy + 2*edge, pHD+0x160). _Header_InitTheme sets pHD+0x160 from GetThemePartSize(HP_HEADERITEM, hdc=NULL, state 0, NULL, TS_TRUE).cy, raised to GetThemePosition(part 1, state 0, TMT_MINSIZE 0xd4b).y if that call succeeds. It also queries parts 5, 4 and 7. Wine's uxtheme returns 6x24 for the HP_HEADERITEM call, and TMT_MINSIZE is absent (0x80070490), the same HRESULT as Win10's ExternalGetPosition. The 24 comes from a 6x288 bitmap with ImageCount 12 in Wine's theme. I infer that Wine's theme authors copied Win10's metrics; this is not verified against Win10.

Semantic divergences from Win10, verified by decomp against Wine's draw.c. TS_MIN: Win10 returns the content-margin sum clamped to at least 1; Wine returns the image size (a FIXME at draw.c:731), so the probe shows MIN == TRUE == DRAW for every image part. BorderFill TS_DRAW: Win10 returns 0x80070057; Wine returns 2*bs+1 with S_OK. NULL psz: Win10 returns E_POINTER; Wine does not check it. HTHEME: Win10 uses a 16-bit index plus a 16-bit generation; Wine uses a pointer. High contrast: Win10 OpenThemeData returns NULL unless the app opted in; Wine has no high-contrast handling. IsAppThemed: Win10 also calls IsAppThemedInternal; Wine just calls IsThemeActive.

These match Win10 or Windows-verified Wine tests: OpenThemeData(NULL class) gives NULL with E_POINTER; an unknown class gives NULL with 0x80070490; NULL htheme gives E_HANDLE; a missing property gives 0x80070490; GetThemeSysSize(NULL) falls back to the system metric.

Themed under Wine is the default and works headlessly. wine.inf seeds HKCU ThemeManager with ThemeActive=1 and DllName=light.msstyles. Switching a prefix to themeless is one command: reg add ... /v ThemeActive /d 0. Themeless Wine gives IsThemeActive=0, OpenThemeData NULL with 0x80070490 for every class, and GetThemePartSize(NULL htheme)=E_HANDLE, the same shape as Industrial7's themeless uxtheme. Wine's loader accepts only PACKTHEM_VERSION==3 text-INI themes, so a real Win10 aero.msstyles very probably will not load (inference). Win10's own format is UNKNOWN.

tools/wine_run.sh runs with no DISPLAY (Wine's null driver), and CreateWindowEx fails there: 'no driver could be loaded'. Window-creating tests need a real X server. Xvfb is not installed and Xephyr cannot open a host display, so I got Xvfb without root (apt-get download xvfb, then dpkg -x into the scratchpad) and wrote run_probe.sh --xvfb. It starts a private Xvfb on a random display, uses a throw-away prefix copy, and tears everything down. Afterwards the X11-unix socket count was 43 before and after, with no stray Xvfb, wineserver or prefix directories.

Wine's own tests do run. Proton is configured --disable-tests, so I built them out of tree from the 11.18 source (flex and bison fetched without root; make took 4.7 s). uxtheme_test: 22254 tests, 3 failures, 16 todo, 4 skipped. Two failures are environmental: aero.msstyles vs light.msstyles naming, and the missing immersive-colour exports. The third (DrawThemeParentBackground sends WM_ERASEBKGND and WM_PRINTCLIENT where the test expects none) I did not isolate. On system wine 9.0 uxtheme_test shows the same 3 failures and then crashes with a page fault after the immersive-colour test. comctl32 header: 1053 tests, 0 failures. button: 76 failures and tab: 11 failures, all focus and window-manager noise under bare Xvfb. Wine has no themed-header-height test anywhere.
